/-!
# Conjecture 9.6

by V. A. Gorbunov

Is it true that an independent basis of quasiidentities of any finite group is finite?

A *quasi-identity* in the signature of groups is a universal Horn sentence
$$\forall \bar x\ \bigl(t_1(\bar x) = s_1(\bar x) \wedge \dots \wedge t_k(\bar x) = s_k(\bar x)
\to t(\bar x) = s(\bar x)\bigr), \qquad k \ge 0,$$
where the $t_i, s_i, t, s$ are group words. The *quasi-identities of a group* $G$ are the
quasi-identities that hold in $G$. A set $B$ of quasi-identities is a *basis* of the
quasi-identities of $G$ if the groups satisfying $B$ are exactly the groups satisfying all
quasi-identities of $G$ (that is, $B$ axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by $G$), and $B$ is
*independent* if no member of $B$ is a consequence of the remaining members (equivalently, no
proper subset of $B$ is a basis).

Which finite groups have a *finite* basis of quasi-identities was settled by Ol'shanskii.
Problem 9.6 asks instead whether a finite group can have an infinite *independent* basis.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

blocks.code:
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premises $t_1 = s_1, \dots, t_k = s_k$, as pairs of words $(t_i, s_i)$. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $t = s$, as the pair of words $(t, s)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ
blocks.docstring:
A quasi-identity in the signature of groups,
$$\forall \bar x\ \bigl(t_1 = s_1 \wedge \dots \wedge t_k = s_k \to t = s\bigr), \qquad k \ge 0.$$
The premises $t_i = s_i$ and the conclusion $t = s$ are equations between group words in the
variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group word is represented by the element of the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` it defines, since two words take the same value in every group under every
assignment of the variables exactly when they define the same element of the free group.
The case $k = 0$ is an identity.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language` / `FirstOrder.Language.Sentence` (Mathlib only provides ring/field languages, no group language, and no notion of Horn/quasi-identity shape); `FreeGroup` (used as the term representation).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.6».QuasiIdentity
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a quasi-identity (universal Horn sentence ∀x̄ (t₁=s₁ ∧ … ∧ tₖ=sₖ → t=s), k ≥ 0) in the signature of groups. Encoded as a `Finset` of premise equations plus a conclusion equation, each equation being a pair of elements of `FreeGroup ℕ` (group words in variables x₀, x₁, … modulo the group laws).

blocks.name: QuasiIdentity
blocks.text:
/--
A quasi-identity in the signature of groups,
$$\forall \bar x\ \bigl(t_1 = s_1 \wedge \dots \wedge t_k = s_k \to t = s\bigr), \qquad k \ge 0.$$
The premises $t_i = s_i$ and the conclusion $t = s$ are equations between group words in the
variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group word is represented by the element of the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` it defines, since two words take the same value in every group under every
assignment of the variables exactly when they define the same element of the free group.
The case $k = 0$ is an identity.
-/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premises $t_1 = s_1, \dots, t_k = s_k$, as pairs of words $(t_i, s_i)$. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $t = s$, as the pair of words $(t, s)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

blocks.docstring:
The quasi-identity `q` holds in the group `H`: for every assignment `x : ℕ → H` of the
variables under which all premises $t_i(\bar x) = s_i(\bar x)$ hold, the conclusion
$t(\bar x) = s(\bar x)$ holds as well.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Sentence.Realize` (would require a group language and Structure instances for groups, which Mathlib lacks).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.6».QuasiIdentity.Holds
justification.why_needed: Satisfaction of a quasi-identity in a group `H`: for every assignment `x : ℕ → H` under which all premises hold (via `FreeGroup.lift x`), the conclusion holds.

blocks.name: Holds
blocks.text:
/--
The quasi-identity `q` holds in the group `H`: for every assignment `x : ℕ → H` of the
variables under which all premises $t_i(\bar x) = s_i(\bar x)$ hold, the conclusion
$t(\bar x) = s(\bar x)$ holds as well.
-/
def Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → H, (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
    FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

blocks.code:
def IsConsequence (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], (∀ p ∈ B, p.Holds H) → q.Holds H
blocks.docstring:
The quasi-identity `q` is a consequence of the set `B` of quasi-identities: every group in
which all members of `B` hold is a group in which `q` holds.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelsBoundedFormula` (`⊨ᵇ`), not usable without a group language.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.6».QuasiIdentity.IsConsequence
justification.why_needed: Semantic consequence within the class of groups: every group (in `Type`) satisfying all of `B` satisfies `q`.

blocks.name: IsConsequence
blocks.text:
/--
The quasi-identity `q` is a consequence of the set `B` of quasi-identities: every group in
which all members of `B` hold is a group in which `q` holds.
-/
def IsConsequence (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], (∀ p ∈ B, p.Holds H) → q.Holds H

blocks.code:
def IsBasisOf (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ B, q.Holds G) ∧ ∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → IsConsequence B q
blocks.docstring:
The set `B` is a basis of the quasi-identities of the group `G`: every member of `B` holds in
`G`, and every quasi-identity holding in `G` is a consequence of `B`. Equivalently, the groups
satisfying `B` are exactly the groups satisfying all quasi-identities of `G`, i.e. `B`
axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by `G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (no quasivariety / axiomatization notions).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.6».QuasiIdentity.IsBasisOf
justification.why_needed: `B` is a basis of the quasi-identities of `G`: every member of `B` holds in `G`, and every quasi-identity holding in `G` is a consequence of `B`; equivalently Mod(B) is the quasivariety generated by `G`.

blocks.name: IsBasisOf
blocks.text:
/--
The set `B` is a basis of the quasi-identities of the group `G`: every member of `B` holds in
`G`, and every quasi-identity holding in `G` is a consequence of `B`. Equivalently, the groups
satisfying `B` are exactly the groups satisfying all quasi-identities of `G`, i.e. `B`
axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by `G`.
-/
def IsBasisOf (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ B, q.Holds G) ∧ ∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → IsConsequence B q

blocks.code:
def Independent (B : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ B, ¬ IsConsequence (B \ {q}) q
blocks.docstring:
The set `B` of quasi-identities is independent: no member of `B` is a consequence of the
remaining members. For a basis `B`, this says exactly that no proper subset of `B` is a basis.

justification.name: Kourovka.«9.6».QuasiIdentity.Independent
justification.why_needed: Independence (irredundancy) of a set of quasi-identities: no member is a consequence of the remaining members.

blocks.name: Independent
blocks.text:
/--
The set `B` of quasi-identities is independent: no member of `B` is a consequence of the
remaining members. For a basis `B`, this says exactly that no proper subset of `B` is a basis.
-/
def Independent (B : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ B, ¬ IsConsequence (B \ {q}) q

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_comm_iff (H : Type*) [Group H] :
    Holds ⟨∅, (FreeGroup.of 0 * FreeGroup.of 1, FreeGroup.of 1 * FreeGroup.of 0)⟩ H ↔
      Std.Commutative (α := H) (· * ·) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun a b ↦ ?_⟩
    simpa using h (fun i ↦ if i = 0 then a else b) (by simp)
  · intro h x _
    simpa using h.comm (x 0) (x 1)
blocks.docstring: The identity $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ holds in a group `H` if and only if `H` is commutative.

      Std.Commutative (α := H) (· * ·) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun a b ↦ ?_⟩
    simpa using h (fun i ↦ if i = 0 then a else b) (by simp)
  · intro h x _

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_multiplicative_int :
    Holds ⟨{(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)}, (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)⟩ (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro x h
  have := h _ (Finset.mem_singleton_self _)
  simp only [map_pow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, map_one] at this ⊢
  exact (pow_eq_one_iff_left two_ne_zero).mp this
blocks.docstring: The quasi-identity $x_0^2 = 1 \to x_0 = 1$ holds in `ℤ` (written multiplicatively).

theorem not_holds_multiplicative_zmod_two :
    ¬ Holds ⟨{(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)}, (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)⟩ (Multiplicative (ZMod 2)) := by
  intro h
  have := h (fun _ ↦ Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (by decide)

claims.decomposer_note: Read with two implicit universal quantifiers: for every finite group G and every independent (irredundant) basis B of the quasi-identities of G (i.e. quasi-identities in the group signature axiomatizing the quasivariety generated by G, no proper subset of which does so), B is finite; this is not the existence question 'does G have a finite quasi-identity basis' (settled by Ol'shanskii), and the answer(sorry) ↔ form fits the existing Kourovka files.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful shape `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (B : Set QuasiIdentity), basis → independent → B.Finite`, with both implicit universal quantifiers after answer(sorry), consequence taken modulo the group axioms, and identities allowed (k = 0). The encoding differences between candidates (FreeGroup ℕ vs syntactic terms; `s = t` vs `w = 1` premises; Finset vs List; Mod(B) = Mod(Q(G)) vs `B ⊆ Q(G) ∧ Q(G) ⊆ Cn(B)`; per-member vs proper-subset independence; models ranging over `Type`) are all provably immaterial to the cardinality question: independent bases inject into logical-equivalence classes, the two basis notions coincide since G ⊨ Q(G), the two independence notions coincide for bases, and a failing quasi-identity reflects to a countable subgroup so universe-0 models suffice. c05 chosen for the clearest docstrings (explicitly distinguishing the problem from Ol'shanskii's finite-basis question), standard `s = t` premise form, and the most thorough proved API/tests (trivial group, commutativity identity iff commutative, a quasi-identity holding in ℤ and failing in ℤ/2). I added c07/c08's `isBasisOf_setOf_holds` API lemma; otherwise the declaration is c05's.

namespace Kourovka.«9.6»

/--
A quasi-identity in the signature of groups,
$$\forall \bar x\ \bigl(t_1 = s_1 \wedge \dots \wedge t_k = s_k \to t = s\bigr), \qquad k \ge 0.$$
The premises $t_i = s_i$ and the conclusion $t = s$ are equations between group words in the
variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; a group word is represented by the element of the free group
`FreeGroup ℕ` it defines, since two words take the same value in every group under every
assignment of the variables exactly when they define the same element of the free group.
The case $k = 0$ is an identity.
-/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The premises $t_1 = s_1, \dots, t_k = s_k$, as pairs of words $(t_i, s_i)$. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The conclusion $t = s$, as the pair of words $(t, s)$. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ

namespace QuasiIdentity

/--
The quasi-identity `q` holds in the group `H`: for every assignment `x : ℕ → H` of the
variables under which all premises $t_i(\bar x) = s_i(\bar x)$ hold, the conclusion
$t(\bar x) = s(\bar x)$ holds as well.
-/
def Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (H : Type*) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → H, (∀ p ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x p.1 = FreeGroup.lift x p.2) →
    FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.1 = FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion.2

/--
The quasi-identity `q` is a consequence of the set `B` of quasi-identities: every group in
which all members of `B` hold is a group in which `q` holds.
-/
def IsConsequence (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (q : QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (H : Type) [Group H], (∀ p ∈ B, p.Holds H) → q.Holds H

/--
The set `B` is a basis of the quasi-identities of the group `G`: every member of `B` holds in
`G`, and every quasi-identity holding in `G` is a consequence of `B`. Equivalently, the groups
satisfying `B` are exactly the groups satisfying all quasi-identities of `G`, i.e. `B`
axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by `G`.
-/
def IsBasisOf (B : Set QuasiIdentity) (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  (∀ q ∈ B, q.Holds G) ∧ ∀ q : QuasiIdentity, q.Holds G → IsConsequence B q

/--
The set `B` of quasi-identities is independent: no member of `B` is a consequence of the
remaining members. For a basis `B`, this says exactly that no proper subset of `B` is a basis.
-/
def Independent (B : Set QuasiIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ q ∈ B, ¬ IsConsequence (B \ {q}) q

/-- Every quasi-identity holds in the trivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_unit (q : QuasiIdentity) : q.Holds Unit :=
  fun _ _ ↦ Subsingleton.elim _ _

/-- The identity $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ holds in a group `H` if and only if `H` is commutative. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_comm_iff (H : Type*) [Group H] :
    Holds ⟨∅, (FreeGroup.of 0 * FreeGroup.of 1, FreeGroup.of 1 * FreeGroup.of 0)⟩ H ↔
      Std.Commutative (α := H) (· * ·) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    refine ⟨fun a b ↦ ?_⟩
    simpa using h (fun i ↦ if i = 0 then a else b) (by simp)
  · intro h x _
    simpa using h.comm (x 0) (x 1)

/-- The quasi-identity $x_0^2 = 1 \to x_0 = 1$ holds in `ℤ` (written multiplicatively). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem holds_multiplicative_int :
    Holds ⟨{(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)}, (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)⟩ (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro x h
  have := h _ (Finset.mem_singleton_self _)
  simp only [map_pow, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, map_one] at this ⊢
  exact (pow_eq_one_iff_left two_ne_zero).mp this

/-- The quasi-identity $x_0^2 = 1 \to x_0 = 1$ fails in the group of order two. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem not_holds_multiplicative_zmod_two :
    ¬ Holds ⟨{(FreeGroup.of 0 ^ 2, 1)}, (FreeGroup.of 0, 1)⟩ (Multiplicative (ZMod 2)) := by
  intro h
  have := h (fun _ ↦ Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) (by decide)
  simp at this

/-- The set of all quasi-identities of a group `G` is a basis of the quasi-identities of `G`. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem isBasisOf_setOf_holds (G : Type*) [Group G] : IsBasisOf {q | q.Holds G} G :=
  ⟨fun _ hq ↦ hq, fun q hq _ _ hB ↦ hB q hq⟩

end QuasiIdentity

/--
Is it true that an independent basis of quasi-identities of any finite group is finite?

That is: for every finite group $G$ and every independent basis $B$ of the quasi-identities
of $G$, is $B$ finite?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.6» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G] (B : Set QuasiIdentity),
      QuasiIdentity.IsBasisOf B G → QuasiIdentity.Independent B → B.Finite := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.6»

items: Terms are represented as elements of `FreeGroup ℕ` (group words modulo the group laws) rather than raw first-order terms in the signature (·, ⁻¹, 1). Since a term and its reduced word take the same value in every group under every assignment, satisfaction, consequence, basis and independence are unchanged; and an independent basis of syntactic quasi-identities maps injectively onto an independent basis in this encoding (two members with the same encoding would be equivalent, contradicting independence), so the cardinality question is the same in both encodings.

Premises are a `Finset` of equations (order and repetition are semantically irrelevant), and the empty premise set (k = 0, i.e. identities) is allowed, following the usual convention that identities are quasi-identities. Requiring k ≥ 1 would give an equivalent finiteness question, since an identity t = s is equivalent over groups to (x₀ = x₀ → t = s).

Consequence is taken within the class of groups (group axioms assumed), as in the theory of quasivarieties of groups; the groups witnessing (non-)consequence are quantified over `Type`. This is faithful because a quasi-identity failing in a group already fails in the countable subgroup generated by the finitely many witnessing elements, and quasi-identities are preserved under subgroups.

`IsBasisOf B G` is stated as (B ⊆ Qid(G)) ∧ (Qid(G) ⊆ Cn(B)); this is equivalent to `Mod(B) = Mod(Qid(G))`, i.e. B axiomatizes the quasivariety generated by G. The first clause is essential (without it e.g. {x₀ = 1} would count as a 'basis' of any group).
`Independent B` is defined as 'no member of B is a consequence of B \ {member}'; for a basis this is equivalent to the decomposition note's 'no proper subset is a basis'.

The finite group is `(G : Type) [Group G] [Finite G]`, matching the style of nearby Kourovka files (20.76). AMS tags 3 (logic), 8 (general algebraic systems / quasivarieties), 20 (group theory) in ascending order.

Four short `@[category test]` lemmas are included as API tests of the bespoke `Holds` definition (trivial group satisfies everything; the commutativity identity holds iff the group is commutative; x₀² = 1 → x₀ = 1 holds in ℤ and fails in ℤ/2).

reviewer_notes: Ambiguities: 'independent basis' read as irredundant (no member is a consequence of the rest), as fixed by the decomposition note; 'basis of quasi-identities of G' read relative to the class of groups (consequence modulo group axioms), the standard convention in Gorbunov/Ol'shanskii. Boundary cases checked: the trivial group is allowed (source says 'any finite group'); it is harmless because, by compactness, any finite group possessing a finite basis has only finite independent bases, so the question is genuinely about finite groups with non-abelian Sylow subgroups. `∅` is never a basis for a finite group (Cn(∅) ≠ Q(G) since G satisfies x^|G| = 1) and is finite anyway. No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised and I found none. Final file compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; `answer(sorry)` renders as `True` in #check, which is the repository elaborator's documented default behaviour.
